question: Given $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & x \end{pmatrix}$, for which value(s) of $x$ will $A^2$ be symmetric?
explanation:
Compute $A^2$.

$A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & x \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & x \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1+0 & 2+2x \\ 0+0 & 0+x^2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2+2x \\ 0 & x^2 \end{pmatrix}$.

For symmetry we must have $a_{12}=a_{21}$.

Thus $2+2x=0 \Rightarrow x=-1$.
